newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece's belt-tightening budget passes parliament.
newsitem.headline: Greece's belt-tightening budget passes parliament.

text.p: The belt-tightening 1997 budget of Greece's ruling socialists was passed by parliament early on Sunday, with Prime Minister Costas Simitis saying it would pave the way for joining a single European currency.
The budget was approved by a vote of 160 to 136 with four absent in the 300-seat parliament. National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou has described the budget as the toughest in 15 years.
Simitis told parliament that cutting large deficits was his priority and "everyone must make sacrifices, especially the wealthy" to ensure Greece's economy was ready for a single European currency.
Failure to achieve full economic integration with Greece's European Union partners would lead to isolation and a national disaster, he said at the end of a five-day debate.

His plan is aimed at cutting the budget deficit to 4.2 percent of gross domestic product in 1997 from 7.6 percent in 1996. It counts largely on raising revenues by adding new taxes, hiking existing taxes and eliminating tax breaks.
